main_text.l: 6. De recessu Regis à
Quàm invitus à Westmonasterio me subduxerim, eorum
esto judicium quos commeatu & armamentis destitutos
Tempestas unquam compulit in altum Mare;
quod tamen potius faciendum, quàm ut oram
legentes, littori, cum Naufragii periculo, al-
lidantur.
Perstiti tamen usque in Alba Aula dum
pudore magis quàm metu pellerer, cùm eum
barbarum furorem, & audaciam Tumultuan-
tium cernerem, ut jam quidvis impudenter
exposcerent, nullâ mihi relictâ nec ipsis Par-
lamenti Membris, Rationis aut Conscientiæ,
libertate, quâ illis quicquam omnino nega-rcutis[?].
Unde nec mihi soli hæc Injuria illata est,
quamquam mihi præcipuè intoleranda; ferre
enim sècunque poterant Proceres, cæterique
Depurati, (si libertate suffragandi sibi permissâ,
minori postea numero vincerentur.
Eorum vero omnium concordantia suffra-
gantium nulla Lex aut Ratio permittit, ut judicium

page.notes: The Q of the opening word is a large decorative initial, read as Quàm. Line "allidantur" is partly obscured at the line end; reconstructed from context. The end of the word "negarem" at the line end is damaged; the visible letters are given as read, with [?]. The catchword "meum" is blurred and given with [?]. "(si" is uncertain at the parenthesis. Running head Greek transcribed in Greek letters as printed. Printed "poltea" read as postea.
